The Sinjar massacre ( ___E:Kurdish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdish_language)___ : Komkujiya Şengalê ) marked the beginning of the ___E:genocide of Yazidis by ISIL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide_of_Yazidis_by_ISIL)___ , the killing and abduction of thousands    of ___E:Yazidi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ men, women and children.

It took place in August 2014 in ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ city and ___E:Sinjar District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_District)___ in Iraq's ___E:Nineveh Governorate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nineveh_Governorate)___ and was perpetrated by the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ (ISIL).

The massacre began with ISIL attacking and capturing Sinjar and neighboring towns on 3 August, during its ___E:Northern Iraq offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Iraq_offensive_(August_2014))___ .

On 8 August 2014, the United States and the United Kingdom responded with airstrikes on ISIL units and convoys in northern ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ , which led to ___E:a military intervention from several countries against ISIL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_intervention_against_the_Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ .

On 17 December 2014, the ___E:Kurdish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdish_people)___ ___E:Peshmerga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshmerga)___ , ___E:PKK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PKK)___ and ___E:YPG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units)___ forces started the ___E:December 2014 Sinjar offensive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/December_2014_Sinjar_offensive)___ with the support of US and British airstrikes.

This offensive broke ISIL's troop transport routes and supply lines between ___E:Mosul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosul)___ and ___E:Raqqa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raqqa)___ , the largest cities in the hands of ISIL at the time.

According to Noori Abdulrahman, the head of the Department of Coordination and Follow-up of the ___E:Kurdistan Regional Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Regional_Government)___ , ISIL wanted to push most of the Kurds out of strategic areas and bring in Arabs who were obedient to ISIL.

Sinjar was predominantly inhabited by ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ before the arrival of the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ .

On 29 June 2014, the Islamic State declared a ___E:caliphate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caliphate)___ in the contiguous areas of ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ and ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ it controlled, after it had made significant advances in northern Iraq during the ___E:Northern Iraq offensive (June 2014) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Iraq_offensive_(June_2014))___ .

After Iraqi federal military forces fled from the advancing ISIL troops, local residents seized their abandoned weapons in case of an attack by the Islamic State.  ___E:Kurdistan Regional Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Regional_Government)___ ___E:Peshmerga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshmerga)___ fighters then moved into and took control of much of the abandoned territory in northern ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ from their stronghold in the ___E:Kurdistan Region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Region)___ .
The Peshmerga confiscated the weapons the Iraqi Army had abandoned, assuring residents that they would protect them.

As ISIL attacked ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ and neighboring cities, the Iraqi Kurdish Peshmerga fighters in Sinjar abandoned the city, leaving the civilians behind without warning.

There is general agreement that the majority of the forces in Shingal on that day were affiliated with the ___E:KDP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Democratic_Party)___ , despite wildly varying estimates as to troop levels.

KDP commanders claim that there were 2,000–4,000 KDP troops in the area. Similarly, Shex Alo, the KDP frontline commander for Shingal section, claims that there were 2,000 KDP fighters in the area, along with one additional Peshmerga brigade and PUK units.

Meanwhile, most others, including but not limited to ___E:HPÊ U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%8Az%C3%AEdxan_Protection_Force)___ commander ___E:Haydar Shesho U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haydar_Shesho)___ and Senior ___E:Gorran Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gorran_Movement)___ official Mustafa Saed Qadir who was the Minister of Peshmerga Affairs at the time and had some Peshmerga brigades in Shingal under his control, estimate that there were many more, around 11,000–15,000 troops stationed.
The villagers defended themselves with their own weapons, but ISIL fighters shelled them with mortars.
By 3 a.m., ISIL fighters had broken through, and began killing anyone seen outdoors.

Sunni militants of the ___E:Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State_of_Iraq_and_the_Levant)___ (ISIL) continued to advance northwards of ___E:Al-Ba'aj U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Ba%27aj)___ towards Sinjar.

On the morning of 3 August 2014, ___E:ISIL U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISIL)___ forces captured the city of ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___  as well as the Sinjar area.  ISIL then detonated the ___E:Sayyidah Zaynab Mosque U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sayyidah_Zaynab_Mosque_(Sinjar))___ in ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ , executed resisters, and demanded the residents swear allegiance and convert to Islam or be killed.
In the surrounding villages, many residents fled immediately.

According to Yazidis, ISIL fighters asked the remaining Yazidis to convert to Islam or face death, and ISIL ___E:Twitter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter)___ accounts posted images of murders in the Sinjar area.

Almost 200,000 civilians, mostly ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ along with ___E:Shia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia)___ , managed to flee from the fighting in ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ city.

About 50,000 Yazidis fled into the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ ,  where they were trapped without food, water or medical care  and faced starvation and dehydration.

The U.S. government, Kurdish ___E:Peshmerga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshmerga)___ forces, and Western media reported that thousands of Yazidis in the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ were under siege by ISIL.

___E:Tahseen Said U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tahseen_Said)___ , the emir of the Yazidis, issued an appeal to world leaders on 3 August 2014, asking for humanitarian help to aid those who were besieged by ISIL.  On 4 August, Kurdish fighters reportedly battled ISIL to retake Sinjar.

On 7 August 2014, The New York Times reported that ISIL had executed dozens of Yazidi men in ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ city and had taken their wives for forced marriage.
It was also reported that ISIL fighters executed ten caretakers of the ___E:Shia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shia)___ Sayeda Zeinab shrine in Sinjar before blowing it up.

While the siege of Mount Sinjar was continuing, ISIL killed hundreds of Yazidis in at least six of the nearby villages. 250–300 men were killed in the village of ___E:Hardan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardan_(Iraq))___ , 200 between Adnaniya and Jazeera, 70–90 in ___E:Qiniyeh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qiniyeh)___ , and on the road out of al-Shimal witnesses reported seeing dozens of bodies.
Hundreds of others had also been killed for refusing to convert to Islam.
On 15 August 2014, in the Yazidi village of ___E:Kocho U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kocho_(Iraq))___ , south of Sinjar, over 80 men were killed after refusing to convert to Islam.

A witness recounted that the villagers were first converted under duress,  According to reports from survivors interviewed by ___E:OHCHR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OHCHR)___ , on 15 August, the entire male population of the Yazidi village of Kocho, up to 400 men, were rounded up and shot by ISIL, and up to 1,000 women and children were abducted.
On the same day, up to 200 Yazidi men were reportedly executed for refusing conversion in a Tal Afar prison.

The massacres took place at least until 25 August when ISIL executed 14 elderly Yazidi men in ___E:Sheikh Mand U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheikh_Mand)___ Shrine in ___E:Jidala U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jidala&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , western Sinjar, and blew up the shrine there.
A civilian reported that on 3 August 2014 alone, 2,000 Yazidis had been killed throughout the ___E:Sinjar District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_District)___ .

A Yazidi member of the ___E:Council of Representatives of Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Representatives_of_Iraq)___ said that between 2 and 5 August 500 Yazidi men had been killed in the city of ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ by ISIL, women had been killed or sold into slavery, and 70 children had died from thirst or suffocation while fleeing the ISIL advance.

From the findings of a joint October 2014 report of the ___E:OHCHR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_the_High_Commissioner_for_Human_Rights)___ and ___E:UNAMI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Assistance_Mission_for_Iraq)___ ,  ISIL had massacred up to 5,000 Yazidi men during August 2014.  ___E:Kurdistan Region U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Region)___ estimated in December 2014 that the total number of killed or missing Yazidi men, women and children from Sinjar since August amounted to around 4,000.
A 2017 report by the ___E:PLOS Medical Journal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PLOS_Medicine)___ estimated between 2,100 and 4,400 deaths and 4,200 to 10,800 abductions.

40,000 or more ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ were trapped in the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ and mostly surrounded by ISIL forces  who were firing on them.  They were largely without food, water or medical care,  facing starvation and dehydration.
On 5 August 2014, Iraqi military helicopters reportedly dropped some food and water for the Yazidis in the mountains.
The US began their own supply drops on 7 August and the UK participated 3 days later.
French aid was also promised.
On 12 August, an Iraqi military helicopter, piloted by Maj. Gen.
Majid Abdul Salam Ashour, crashed in the mountains while delivering aid and rescuing stranded Yazidi refugees.
The general was killed in the crash,  while most of the passengers, including Iraqi MP ___E:Vian Dakhil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vian_Dakhil)___ , were injured.
On 13 August, a 16-aircraft mission including US C-17s and C-130Hs, an Australian C-130J, and a British C-130J delivered supplies to mostly Yezidi civilians stranded on Mount Sinjar.

On 7 August 2014, the U.S. president, ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , stated that the U.S. was starting air strikes to prevent a potential massacre ( ___E:genocide U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genocide)___ ) by ISIL of thousands of ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ trapped in the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ .
Obama further defended his decision by saying:
The world is confronted by many challenges.
And while America has never been able to right every wrong, America has made the world a more secure and prosperous place.
And our leadership is necessary to underwrite the global security and prosperity that our children and our grandchildren will depend upon. We do so by adhering to a set of core principles.
We do whatever is necessary to protect our people.
We support our allies when they're in danger.
We lead coalitions of countries to uphold international norms.

And we strive to stay true to the fundamental values – the desire to live with basic freedom and dignity – that is common to human beings wherever they are. That's why people all over the world look to the United States of America to lead. And that's why we do it.
On 8 August 2014, US airstrikes were launched in the ___E:Erbil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erbil)___ area, 180 km east of Sinjar.
The first airstrikes in the Mount Sinjar area were reported on 9 August, when the US launched four strikes against armored fighting vehicles of ISIL fighters threatening civilians on Mount Sinjar.
The continued Iraqi airdrops of food and water in the Sinjar Mountains and their picking up of some Yazidis were also backed up by the U.S. airstrikes.
After the air strikes, the U.S. government spent five days discussing the possibilities and necessity of a rescue operation with U.S. ground troops or U.S. airlifts.

Between 9  and 11 August 2014,  a safe corridor was established from the mountain enabling 10,000 people to evacuate on the first day.  Kurdish fighters of ___E:Kurdistan Workers' Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Workers%27_Party)___ (PKK) entered the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ with trucks and tractors to carry out the sick and elderly into Syria via a path that was cleared by Syrian Kurdish militants ( ___E:YPG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units)___ ).

According to Dr. Salim Hassan, a professor at the university of ___E:Sulaymaniyah U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulaymaniyah)___ and spokesman of the uprooted Yazidis, the ___E:PKK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurdistan_Workers%27_Party)___ and YPG enabled an estimated 35,000 of the initially 50,000 trapped Yazidis to escape into Syria.
According to the account of the Sinjar District Governor, the route was jointly set up by Peshmerga and the YPG.
On 12  or 13 August 2014, a dozen U.S.

Marines and special forces servicemen landed on Mount Sinjar from CH-53E aircraft to assess options for a potential rescue of Yazidi refugees joining British SAS already in the area.   They reported that "the situation is much more manageable", that there were now far fewer Yazidis on the mountain than expected, and that those Yazidis were in relatively good condition.
A U.S. rescue mission for those still on the mountain was therefore "far less likely now", said Defense Secretary ___E:Chuck Hagel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Hagel)___ .

The U.S. government officially declared the siege to be broken on 13 August 2014. This was reportedly done by U.S. airstrikes and Kurdish fighters of the ___E:People's Protection Units U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units)___ from Syria, together with their ___E:PKK U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PKK)___ allies from Turkey,   allowing more than 50,000 refugees to escape.
Despite this, according to Professor Salim Hassan, between 5,000 and 10,000 people still remained trapped in the mountains.
They were reportedly afraid to return to their homes and were sustained in the coming months by airdrops from a lone Iraqi helicopter.
On 7 August 2014, U.S.
President Obama ordered targeted airstrikes on IS militants and emergency air relief for the Yazidis.

Airstrikes began on 8 August. (See ___E:American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021) § Obama authorizes airstrikes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American-led_intervention_in_Iraq_(2014%E2%80%932021)#Obama_authorizes_airstrikes)___ .)
On 8 August 2014, the US asserted that the systematic destruction of the Yazidi people by the Islamic State was genocide.
President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ had authorized the attacks to protect Yazidis but also Americans and Iraqi minorities.
President Obama gave an assurance that no troops would be deployed for combat.
Along with the airstrikes of 9 August, the US ___E:airdropped U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airdrop)___ 3,800 gallons of water and 16,128 ___E:MREs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MRE)___ .
Following these actions, the United Kingdom and France stated that they also would begin airdrops.
On 10 August 2014, at approximately 2:15 a.m.
ET, the US carried out five additional airstrikes on armed vehicles and a mortar position, enabling 20,000–30,000 Yazidi Iraqis to flee into Syria and later be rescued by Kurdish forces.
The Kurdish forces then provided shelter for the Yazidis in ___E:Dohuk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dohuk)___ .

On 13 August 2014, fewer than 20 ___E:United States Special Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Special_Forces)___ troops stationed in Irbil along with ___E:Special Air Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_Air_Service)___ troops visited the area near Mount Sinjar to gather intelligence and plan the evacuation of approximately 30,000 Yazidis still trapped on Mount Sinjar.
One hundred and twenty-nine additional US military personnel were deployed to Irbil to assess and provide a report to President Obama.

The United States Central Command also reported that a seventh airdrop was conducted and that to date, 114,000 meals and more than 35,000 gallons of water had been airdropped to the displaced Yazidis in the area.

In a statement on 14 August 2014, ___E:The Pentagon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pentagon)___ said that the 20 US personnel who had visited the previous day had concluded that a rescue operation was probably unnecessary since there was less danger from exposure or dehydration and the Yazidis were no longer believed to be at risk of attack from ISIL. Estimates also stated that 4,000 to 5,000 people remained on the mountain, with nearly half of them being Yazidi ___E:herders U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herder)___ who lived there before the siege.

Kurdish officials and Yazidi refugees stated that thousands of young, elderly, and disabled individuals on the mountain were still vulnerable, with the governor of Kurdistan's ___E:Dahuk province U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dahuk)___ , ___E:Farhad Atruchi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Farhad_Atruchi&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , saying that the assessment was "not correct" and that although people were suffering, "the international community is not moving".
After August 2014, ISIL held the town of ___E:Sinjar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar)___ .

Several thousand  ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ remained in the ___E:Sinjar Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinjar_Mountains)___ located to the city's north, sustained by airdrops from a lone Iraqi helicopter,  while an escape road from the mountains northward to Kurdish areas was under Kurdish/Yazidi control.

American officials said that some of those Yazidis considered the Sinjar Mountains a place of refuge and home and did not want to leave;  while a report from The New Yorker said some were afraid to return to their homes.
Other Yazidis also came to the mountains after the August evacuations.
On 21 October 2014, ISIL seized territory to the north of the mountains, cutting the area's escape route to Kurdish areas.
The Yazidi militias then withdrew into the Sinjar Mountains, where the number of Yazidi civilian refugees was estimated at 2,000–7,000.  The mountains had once again been partially besieged by ISIL.

On 17 December 2014, ___E:Peshmerga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshmerga)___ forces, backed by 50 U.S.-led coalition airstrikes on ISIL positions, launched an offensive to liberate Sinjar  and to break the partial siege of the Sinjar Mountains.
In less than two days, the Peshmerga seized the mountain range.
After ISIL forces retreated, Kurdish fighters were initially faced with clearing out mines in the area,  but quickly opened a land corridor that enabled Yazidis to be evacuated.
The operation left 100 ISIL fighters dead.

Late on 21 December 2014, Syrian Kurdish ___E:YPG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units)___ fighters south of the mountain range reached Peshmerga lines, thus linking their two fronts.
The next day, the YPG broke through ISIL lines, thus opening a corridor from ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ to the town of Sinjar.
By the evening, the Peshmerga took control of much of Sinjar.

Following ISIL's retreat from Iraqi and Kurdish forces in the region during late-2017 campaigns, both governments laid claim to the area. The Yazidi population, with only about 15% returning to Sinjar during the period, was caught in the political crossfire.
Yazidis returned to an abandoned town of crumbling buildings, leftover IEDs and the remains of those killed during the massacre.
In November 2017, a mass grave of about 70 people was uncovered [citation needed] and a month later in December, another mass grave was discovered holding about 90 victims.

According to the ___E:UN Assistance Mission for Iraq (UNAMI) U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Assistance_Mission_for_Iraq)___ and the UN Human Rights Office there are more than 200 mass graves sites across Iraq.  The Documentation Project run by the NGO ___E:Yazda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazda)___ has provided photographic and witness testimony to document dozens of mass grave sites across the Nineveh Plain and Sinjar.

In March 2019, the first mass grave site in Sinjar was exhumed by the Iraqi Mass Graves Directorate within the Martyr's Foundation and the Medical Legal Directorate under the Iraqi Ministry of Health in conjunction with UNITAD (United Nations Investigative Team to Promote Accountability for Crimes Committed by Da'esh/ISIL).
In November 2023, Iraq's Minister of Immigration and Displacement, Ivan Jabru, announced the return of 1,150 displaced Yezidis to Sinjar and expressed hopes that more would return in the near future.
